spec_used: specs/ocr/biology-b-21c-J257.md (+ specs/ocr/biology-b-21c-J257-bold.md as the tier authority)

assessment_verified.structure: Foundation Tier: Breadth in biology (01) and Depth in biology (02). Higher Tier: Breadth (03) and Depth (04). Learners are entered for one tier only.
assessment_verified.chapter_coverage: Both papers assess content from all chapters, so there is no chapter-to-paper split.
assessment_verified.paper_difference: The Depth paper carries the 6-mark extended responses; the Breadth paper does not.
assessment_verified.practical_skills: Practical activities are PAGs. Chapter B2 cites PAG1 (light microscope), PAG6 (pulse and recovery rate) and PAG7 (aseptic technique, antibiotic discs on agar).
assessment_verified.unit_mapping: This unit is Chapter B2 'Keeping healthy', topics B2.1 to B2.6. Lesson 1 covers B2.1.1-B2.1.5 plus B2.2.1, B2.2.3, B2.2.4, B2.2.5 and B2.2.6. Lesson 2 covers B2.3.1, B2.3.2, part of B2.4.1a, and B2.4.4-B2.4.5. Lesson 3 covers B2.5.1a, B2.5.2 and B2.5.3a-d. Lesson 4 covers B2.6.1 and B2.6.4, with antibiotic resistance linked to B6.1.
assessment_verified.separate_only_content_present: Partly. B2.2.3 and B2.2.6 (plant physical and chemical defences) are taught in lesson 1, and B2.4.4-B2.4.5 (monoclonal antibodies in diagnosis) in lesson 2. B2.4.1b, B2.4.2, B2.4.3 and B2.6.5 are taught nowhere - see F15 and F16.
assessment_verified.higher_tier_only_in_B2: Only two runs of the chapter are bold: the B2.4 monoclonal antibody narrative with outcomes B2.4.4 and B2.4.5, and B2.6.5 (monoclonal antibodies to treat cancer). Everything else in B2 is both tiers.
assessment_verified.wrong_board_wording: Two practice questions were typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method' (AQA and Edexcel wording). No B2.1a-style codes, no 'topic' numbering, no 60 marks / 1 hour 10, no 'Paper 1 covers', no 'core practical'.

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the whole plant-defences paragraph (waxy cuticle, cell wall, antimicrobial substances) inside the 'Plant Defences Against Pathogens (Separate Science)' collapsible.
findings.truth: This content is separate science only, not Higher tier only, so Foundation students of this qualification are assessed on it. The wrapper must come off; body.tier-foundation .higher-only is display:none, so the text was removed, not badged.
findings.evidence: spec B2.2.3 ('describe physical plant defences, including leaf cuticle and cell wall (separate science only)') and B2.2.6 ('describe chemical plant defence responses, including antimicrobial substances (separate science only)') are both plain text in the bold-preserved extraction, so both tiers.

findings.claim: 'Explain why viruses are more difficult to treat than bacterial infections.' is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: The (HT) flag is wrong and tells Foundation students to skip a question they can be set. Drop it.
findings.evidence: spec B2.6.1 (explain the use of medicines, including antibiotics, in the treatment of disease) is not bold; nor is the B2.1 narrative on viruses reproducing inside host cells.

findings.claim: The higher-only wrapper opens one paragraph too early, so the whole 'Identifying Pathogens in the Lab' section - including culturing on nutrient agar, microscopy of colonies and antimicrobial sensitivity testing - is hidden from Foundation students.
findings.truth: Narrow the wrapper so it starts at the monoclonal antibody material. The traditional identification methods are both-tier content and must stay visible; the last sentence of that paragraph only introduces monoclonal antibodies, so leaving it visible costs nothing.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.1a ('describe ways in which diseases, including plant diseases, can be detected and identified, in the lab and in the field') is not bold; the B2.4 monoclonal antibody narrative and outcomes B2.4.4 and B2.4.5 are bold.

findings.claim: 'Describe the steps involved in producing monoclonal antibodies for use in a diagnostic test.' is typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: Wrong on two counts: this board calls its practical activities PAGs, not required practicals, and producing monoclonal antibodies is not a school practical. Retype to '4 marks - Describe a Process', a label already used in this unit.
findings.evidence: spec practical-skills section: practicals are indicated as PAG1, PAG2 and so on. 'Required practical' is AQA and Edexcel wording. B2.4 lists PAG1 and PAG7 as its practicals.

findings.claim: Two practice questions (the rapid monoclonal-antibody diagnostic test; the steps in producing monoclonal antibodies) carry no tier flag.
findings.truth: Both test Higher-tier-only outcomes and need the (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.4 and B2.4.5 are bold.

findings.claim: The knowledge check on why monoclonal antibodies are 'specific' carries no tier flag.
findings.truth: Prefix it with (Higher tier). All five answer keys are correct: index 1 (rapid secondary response), index 1 (one particular antigen), index 2 ('transmission'), index 2 ('disease'), and the match order [1,2,0] pairs antigen, antibody and memory cell correctly.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.4 and B2.4.5 are bold; knowledge checks are not tier-filtered in the player, so the text tag is the only signal a student gets.

findings.claim: Three flashcards (why monoclonal antibodies are specific, the first production step, one diagnostic use) carry no tier tag.
findings.truth: Tag them at the end of the question. The other eight cards are B2.3 vaccination and prevention content and stay untagged.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.4 and B2.4.5 are bold; B2.3.1 and B2.3.2 are not.

findings.claim: The third takeaway states the whole monoclonal antibody outcome with no flag.
findings.truth: Prefix it with (Higher tier). A wrapper cannot go inside the <ul>.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.4 and B2.4.5 are bold.

findings.claim: The exam tip tells every student 'For monoclonal antibody production, you must be able to describe the steps in sequence'.
findings.truth: That is required at Higher tier only. Tag the clause inline; the vaccination advice around it is both tiers and stays as it is.
findings.evidence: spec B2.4.4 is bold; B2.3.2 (use of vaccines) is not.

findings.claim: 'Describe how she could design an epidemiological study...' is typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: Other-board wording again, and designing a cohort study is not a practical activity. Retype to '4 marks - Apply Ideas about Science'.
findings.evidence: spec B2.5.3c (principles of sampling as applied to scientific data, M2d) and the IaS3/IaS4 link 'discuss correlation, cause and risk in the context of non-communicable diseases'.

findings.claim: 'Epidemiology is the study of _____ of disease across populations.' is a gap-fill that names the answer in the question, and the stored answer does not fill the gap.
findings.truth: Reword the question so it matches the answer already stored.
findings.evidence: house rule: flashcard questions must be substantive and must not give the answer away.

findings.claim: The double-blind trial question is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: Clinical trial design is both tiers. Drop the (HT) flag.
findings.evidence: spec B2.6.4 is not bold, and the B2.6 narrative naming open-label, blind and double-blind trials and the ethics of placebos is not bold either.

findings.claim: 'Suggest two ways in which the reliability of the trial could be improved.' is typed '2 marks - Short Calculation'.
findings.truth: There is no calculation in the question or the mark scheme. Retype to '2 marks - Apply Ideas about Science'.
findings.evidence: the item's own scheme awards a mark each for sample size, blinding, randomisation or trial duration; no arithmetic is asked for anywhere in it.

findings.claim: 'MRSA stands for _____ and is notable because ___.' carries two gaps in two different formats and cannot be answered as written.
findings.truth: Reword to a question that matches the stored answer.
findings.evidence: house rule: flashcard questions must be substantive and answerable.

findings.claim: Six both-tier B2 outcomes are taught in no lesson: B2.2.2 (platelets), B2.4.1b (use a light microscope to observe microorganisms, PAG1), B2.4.2 (aseptic techniques, PAG7), B2.4.3 and B2.6.2 (calculate cross-sectional areas of cultures and clear zones with pi r squared, M5c, PAG7), B2.5.1b (investigate the effect of exercise on pulse rate and recovery rate, PAG6), B2.5.4 (interactions between different types of disease) and B2.6.3 (evaluate treatments for cardiovascular disease, including lifestyle changes, medicines and surgery).
findings.truth: All are assessable at both tiers and three of them carry PAGs, against a paper guarantee that no less than 15 per cent of the questions assess practical skills. Options: (a) add a practical section to lesson 2 covering aseptic technique, agar plates and the clear-zone area calculation, a pulse-and-recovery paragraph to lesson 3, and a cardiovascular-treatment section to lesson 4 - about three sections and three practice questions; (b) accept the gaps if the practical skills are taught in this subject's practical-skills unit. Recommend (a): the clear-zone calculation is the only maths skill in the chapter, and B2.6.3 is the chapter's only evaluate-treatments outcome, so both are likely exam questions. B2.5.4 needs only one sentence in lesson 3.
findings.evidence: spec B2.2.2, B2.4.1b, B2.4.2, B2.4.3, B2.5.1b, B2.5.4, B2.6.2, B2.6.3, all plain text in the bold-preserved extraction; assessment section on practical skills weighting.

findings.claim: B2.6.5, monoclonal antibodies used to treat cancer, is taught nowhere. Lesson 2 covers monoclonal antibodies in diagnosis only.
findings.truth: This is separate-science-only and Higher-tier-only content, so it belongs in this subject and it is a genuine hole for Higher candidates. Recommend adding it as a short higher-only block at the end of lesson 4, with the spec's four steps: produce antibodies specific to a cancer cell antigen, inject them, they bind and tag the cancer cells for attack by white blood cells, and they can carry a radioactive or toxic substance to the cancer cell.
findings.evidence: spec B2.6.5 is bold and tagged (separate science only).

findings.claim: Question-type labels do not always match the task: 'Explain how vaccination protects an individual' is typed 'Compare or Contrast' (lesson 2), and so is 'Describe three non-specific defences' (lesson 1).
findings.truth: Both should read Explain or Describe. Left alone here because the retro programme runs question-type relabels as its own sweep, and neither label changes what the mark scheme rewards.
findings.evidence: the items' own mark schemes ask for a mechanism and for three named defences, not for a comparison.

findings.claim: The tooltip on 'receptors' reads 'A protein on or in a cell that a drug binds to in order to produce its effect, for example a receptor, enzyme or ion channel', so it defines a receptor with a receptor.
findings.truth: The definition describes a drug target, not a receptor. The sentence around it is correct and the circularity is not mark-affecting, so it is recorded rather than edited; the glossary entry repeats the same slip.
findings.evidence: settled fact: a receptor is one kind of drug target, alongside enzymes and ion channels.

summary: Four lessons checked against J257 chapter B2. No factual errors: pathogen types and named human and plant diseases match B2.1.4 and B2.1.5, the vaccination and memory-cell mechanism matches B2.2 and B2.3.2, the monoclonal antibody production steps match B2.4.4, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, LDL, BMI, MRSA and the antibiotic-resistance mechanism are all correct, and all twenty knowledge-check keys and four match items are right. The unit's fault is tier flagging, and it runs in both directions. Only two runs of B2 are bold: the monoclonal antibody material in B2.4 and B2.6.5. Lesson 1 wrapped separate-science plant defences as higher-only, deleting both-tier content for Foundation students, and lesson 2 wrapped the both-tier lab identification methods along with the monoclonal ones; meanwhile the genuinely Higher monoclonal questions, checks, flashcards and takeaway carried no tier tag at all, and two both-tier questions carried a wrong (HT) flag. 19 edits fix the two wrappers and tag or untag ten assessment items. Three questions carried other-board or impossible type labels: two 'Required Practical Method' (this board uses PAGs) and one 'Short Calculation' with no calculation. Two coverage gaps referred up: seven both-tier outcomes including three PAGs and the chapter's only maths skill, and B2.6.5 monoclonal antibodies for cancer.
